as_told.title: Imperial College DMT research mapping the spirit world

plain: Around 2015, researchers at Imperial College in London are said to have found a way to keep people in the state brought on by DMT, a powerful psychedelic whose effects usually fade within minutes, for about 30 minutes. A neuroscientist named Andrew Gallimore tells Michels this. He connects the work to the researcher Christopher Timmermann and says the college "developed a much better model" of it. He adds that "all of the subjects at Imperial College got through it" with no serious harm. The writer Graham Hancock, on an earlier episode, says they found a way to keep people in the DMT state "for an hour", and Michels himself calls the work "sort of mapping the spirit world", which is why it matters to them: a longer trip would give more time to explore what people meet there.
